_README: BASELINE OF PRE-EXISTING FAQ / FAQPage JSON-LD DRIFT. This is a RATCHET, not an allowlist.
Recorded 2026-07-31 when the faq-jsonld-parity check was first written. Until then NOTHING in
npm test compared visible FAQ text to the FAQPage structured data, so this drift accumulated
silently. Google reads the JSON-LD and the user reads the DOM; when they disagree the rich
result misrepresents the page, which is a documented rich-result violation.
PAID DOWN IN FULL 2026-08-02: the debt is 0. It was 375 fields across 87 files, plus one
count mismatch (articles/article-washer-repair-irvine.html rendered 5 FAQ items but declared
only 4 in its FAQPage node). Every FAQPage entry site-wide now matches its visible copy
verbatim. See tasks/backlog.md P6-12 and scripts/oneoff/conform-faq-jsonld-2026-08-02.js.
THE FILE STAYS, EMPTY, AS THE ZERO FLOOR. With no entries, any drift on any page fails the
check immediately: an unlisted file with drift is a failure, and every file is now unlisted.
Do not delete this file and do not add entries to it to make a failing run pass. New drift is
a bug in the page, not a number to record here. The only legitimate reason to add an entry
would be a second bulk import of externally-authored pages, and even then it should be paid
down in the same milestone, not banked.
The check FAILS if: a file not listed here has drift; a listed file's count INCREASES; or a
listed file becomes clean but is still listed. That last rule is what stops this file from
rotting into permanent silence - the baseline can only ever shrink.
KNOWN LIMITATION (now moot at zero, kept for the record): the number was a COUNT, not a
content pin. Within a file already listed here, fixing one drifted field while breaking a
previously-clean one netted to zero and passed. At an empty baseline there is nothing to
hide behind: every drifted field is reported on its own.
